label: Shot
definition: A discrete unit of visual narrative with a specified beginning and end. The most generic definition — in some cases a Shot covers an entire Capture, in others only a portion of one.

label: Sequence
definition: An ordered collection of media used to organize units of work. A Sequence, or a rendered version of it, can itself be used as a Shot in another Sequence.

label: Editorial Shot
definition: A Shot for use in an Editorial Sequence. A subclass of Shot with optional detailed timing information added.

label: VFX Shot
definition: A Shot that has been identified as requiring VFX work. Same attributes as a generic Shot.

label: VFX Sequence
definition: A unit of work made up of an ordered series of VFX shots. May not be a continuous narrative — usually created around blocks of related VFX work, so every shot involving one prop can be grouped into one VFX Sequence.

label: VFX Image Sequence
definition: An Image Sequence used in VFX work, for when the process needs individual independent frames. In that case all of the Shots should be Image Sequences rather than Moving Images.

label: Animation Shot
definition: A Shot identified as requiring Animation work. Shots with both live action and animation are categorised as VFX Shots, not Animation Shots.

label: Animation Sequence
definition: A unit of work made up of an ordered series of Animation shots. Unlike VFX Sequences these are usually complete from a narrative perspective, and their content is often decided by editorial.

label: Color Sequence
definition: A sequence of shots with colour grading characteristics linked to creative intent. Grouped by the work rather than by the narrative — foggy dock scenes together, leafy stately-home exteriors together.

label: Sequence Chronology Descriptor
definition: Describes how a series of Shots is used to generate a Sequence. EDL, AAF and OTIO are all subclasses of this general concept. Carries per-shot identifiers and optional source timecodes, record timecodes in the destination, and ancillary metadata such as markers and transition effects.

label: Slate
definition: The virtualized version of the physical slate. How everything gets tied together after shooting is done; its use as connective tissue generally still requires human intervention.

label: Slate UID
definition: A unique way of specifying important details about each camera setup when the camera rolls. Combines the Production Scene Number, Setup and Take into an alphanumeric string. There are conventions for this but no standards — it can be parsed into its components if the conventions being followed are known. Unique within a particular Creative Work.

label: Slate Name
definition: The combination of Scene Descriptor and Setup — the Slate UID without the Take. Loosely, it covers all the Takes of a particular Production Scene using a particular Setup.

label: Setup
definition: The unique camera configuration that encompasses a camera's geo-location, positioning, lens, or other camera settings.

label: Take
definition: A discrete capture event with a specified beginning and end. May include audio, video or motion capture. Usually specified by the director calling a start and end.

label: Capture
definition: An Asset Functional Class. A video Capture, or a processed version of it, is often the source for a Shot. In some circumstances what the Ontology calls a Capture is referred to as a shot — in the Ontology a shot in that sense is a section of a Capture.

label: Camera Unit
definition: A group of Participants responsible for shooting some element of a Production Scene — Main Unit or Second Unit. Usually multiple people but can be a single person.

label: Source Start
definition: Start of the section of the material being used.

label: Source End
definition: End of the section of the material being used.

label: Record Start
definition: The time in the Sequence where this use of the material starts. Named for reasons of history and industry practice.

label: Record End
definition: The time in the Sequence where the content taken from the material ends.
